newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver ends down, gold higher.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver ends down, gold higher.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) prices close 30 rupees lower at 7,410 rupees per kg.
** Higher prices attract profit-taking during the day following weak trend in the world market.
** Gold 24 carat closed 25 rupees higher at 4,825 rupees per 10 gramme on fresh seasonal buying and limited inflow.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) close 300 rupees higher at 56,400 rupees per piece.
Silver (.999) prices ended Thursday 30 rupees lower at 7,410 rupees per kg, dealers said.
They said prices opened lower at 7,410 rupees against Wednesday's close of 7,440 rupees per kg on the back of overnight losses in global markets.
"This prompted light profit-taking in early trade, but stray industrial enquiries later on kept the market quiet at opening levels," one dealer said.
Silver was up by 15 rupees on Wednesday.
"Arrivals were low as landed cost of the imported silver is higher than local prices," another dealer said.
Gold 24 carat closed 25 rupees higher at 4,825 rupees per 10 grammes on wedding season purchases and limited arrivals, dealers said.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes each) closed 300 rupees higher at 56,400 rupees per piece.
Traders said they expected silver to remain weak in the next week on sliding global prices while gold would attract profit-taking at higher levels.
